name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz transits down 40%+; mines hit 24 Nov
summary: Hormuz transits fell over 40% to 125 ships on 17–23 Nov; Iran's navy says two tankers hit mines on 24 Nov
state: Marine Traffic data showed 125 vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz from 17 to 23 Nov, against 226 from 1 to 7 Nov, with only three crossings on 22 Nov; pre-war traffic was 125–140 ships a day (Al Jazeera, 24 Nov). Iran's navy said two tankers struck mines and caught fire on 24 Nov, and its army chief said the strait would be closed further day by day. UKMTO and Vanguard reported repeated projectile strikes on tankers in mid-November, and Iran says only its northern corridor is permitted (Seatrade Maritime). Hormuz traffic stays materially impeded.
for_you: Shipping through the Gulf faces attacks, mines and routing limits, which tends to raise freight and insurance costs and delay deliveries. Seafarers and operators should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories; travellers should check FCDO travel advice for the region.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (125 transits 17–23 Nov vs 125–140 a day pre-war)

sources.title: Al Jazeera — Hormuz oil traffic is down 40 percent: Are Iran's tanker attacks working?
Seatrade Maritime — Tanker confirmed struck in the Gulf, Iran claims VLCC sinking

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
